stem:
In figure 3.48, point A is on the bisector of \(\angle XYZ\). If AX = 2 cm then find AZ.

In the figure, the two arcs marked at the vertex Y show that \(\angle XYA \cong \angle AYZ\); the point X lies on one arm of \(\angle XYZ\) with seg AX \(\perp\) ray YX at X, and the point Z lies on the other arm with seg AZ \(\perp\) ray YZ at Z. Both right angles are marked in the figure.
diagramNote: Fig. 3.48 — angle XYZ with vertex Y; A lies on the bisector ray. Two small arcs at Y mark the two equal angles. Right-angle mark at X (AX perpendicular to ray YX) and at Z (AZ perpendicular to ray YZ).

stem:
In figure 3.49, \(\angle RST = 56^\circ\), seg PT \(\perp\) ray ST, seg PR \(\perp\) ray SR and seg PR \(\cong\) seg PT. Find the measure of \(\angle RSP\). State the reason for your answer.

In the figure, T lies on ray ST and R lies on ray SR, and the point P lies in the interior of \(\angle RST\); the right angles are marked at T and at R.
diagramNote: Fig. 3.49 — vertex S with ray ST above and ray SR below; P is an interior point (shown on a dashed ray from S). Right-angle mark at T (PT perpendicular to ray ST) and at R (PR perpendicular to ray SR).

stem:
In figure 3.50, if seg PR \(\cong\) seg PQ, show that seg PS \(>\) seg PQ.

In the figure, the points Q, R and S are collinear with R lying between Q and S, and seg PQ, seg PR and seg PS are drawn from the point P which is not on line QS. The double tick marks on seg PQ and on seg PR show that these two segments are congruent.
diagramNote: Fig. 3.50 — Q, R, S collinear on one line with R between Q and S; P above the line joined to Q, R and S. Double tick marks on seg PQ and seg PR mark them congruent.

stem:
In figure 3.51, in \(\triangle ABC\), seg AD and seg BE are altitudes and AE = BD.

Prove that seg AD \(\cong\) seg BE.

In the figure, D lies on side BC with seg AD \(\perp\) side BC, and E lies on side AC with seg BE \(\perp\) side AC; both right angles are marked in the figure.
diagramNote: Fig. 3.51 — triangle ABC with B and C on a horizontal base. Altitude AD drawn dashed from A to D on BC with a right-angle mark at D; altitude BE drawn dashed from B to E on AC with a right-angle mark at E.
